title: Latvia Targets Russian and Belarusian Trade With 300% Grain Tariff and… · 12 Sep
keywords: Latvia, Russia, Belarus, grain tariff, import restrictions, sanctions, trade policy, inflation, EU decoupling, Baltic states, economic security, geopolitics
notes: Latvia is imposing a 300% tariff on grain imports from Russia and Belarus and expanding restrictions on a broad range of consumer goods, in what Riga frames as a security-driven decoupling from hostile states. The measures have strong political backing but raise legitimate questions about costs for businesses, logistics workers, and ordinary consumers. With inflation still running above zero and ticking upward in August 2026, the government faces pressure to show that principled trade policy does not come at the expense of household stability.
